reasoning: Multiple independent polls from January-February 2026 consistently show opposition party Tisza leading Fidesz by 8-10 percentage points (around 49% vs 39%). The election is scheduled for April 12, 2026. However, several factors complicate this: 1) Hungary's electoral system favors Fidesz through gerrymandering and institutional control, 2) Orban has consolidated power over 16 years and controls state media, 3) There's speculation Orban may attempt to manipulate results or even cancel elections in some districts, 4) Pro-government polls show different results. While Tisza has strong momentum, especially among youth and urban voters, Orban's structural advantages and willingness to use administrative resources mean the outcome remains uncertain despite polling leads.
